about: What each commit of this hour changed: its message beyond the subject, its session (the Claude-Session trailer), and its files with lines added and removed (git numstat; at most 40 files a commit). Written by tools/agents-commits.mjs. The list of commits: data/agents/commits.json.

ed89c75c4959d94247a4a857b502b3dc84353206.body:
node tools/brief-pdf.mjs --site _site --out <dir> writes brief-latest.pdf and edition-<n>.pdf
(A4 landscape, the page's own print stylesheet; outside requests refused while rendering);
writes only into --out; exits 0 with a warning when Playwright, Chromium or the built page is
missing, or a render fails. --inputs prints the files the PDFs are drawn from (brief/**, the
frame's build, styles and wordmarks, the two brief scripts) and their sha256 key on stderr.
Measured in a session: 3 PDFs (12, 9 and 12 pages) in 3.5 s with Chromium present.

078d643efa01ea8ac1f153c83318381bb2f20fae.body:
closedStrip now reads incident.researcher@'s `scope` on each decision edge: a body listed as closed or as running is marked
"in part" when its edge's extent is "part", and the part itself (`parts`) is the mark's tooltip. "With limits" carries no mark
(partial already). Only an edge with no scope yet keeps the old inference (closed, plus a same-body decision with hours today
that runs). As read on dev now: FlixBus, CP (four bridge trains, 12:00 to 15:00) and Transtejo Soflusa (one route) in part.

7cfb880e148415ee0a90ff8b61d92c8487ab8904.body: Each page reads the operator's own site, feed or open API first and says which. The press appears only where the operator publishes nothing readable: the researcher's decisions, labelled evidence. Metro: Metro de Lisboa's own news (its public WordPress API), Metro do Porto's news pages, MTS's WordPress API. Metro de Lisboa's live line status comes from an internal page endpoint and is not read; its API needs a key, listed for Dinis. New data files: metro.json, buses.json, ferries.json; services.json stays for the broadcast wall. The reader now decodes HTML entities and asks for HTML when it reads a page.
